data.name: Kuldipsinh
data.gender_notes: Kuldipsinh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit words 'kula' meaning 'moon' and 'deep' meaning 'born'. The name Kuldipsinh signifies one who is born under the crescent moon. In Hindu mythology, the moon is considered a symbol of fertility, renewal, and protection. The name Kuldipsinh carries the meaning “Moon-born, crescent moon” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Kuldipsinh usually hope their child will grow to embody moon-born, crescent moon and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: One who is born under the divine and nurturing influence of the moon.
data.etymology: Kuldipsinh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Moon-born, crescent moon.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kuldipsinh total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

historical_references.reference: Kuldipsinh Chauhan was the founder of the Chauhan Rajputs in the late 11th century CE. He is considered to be the progenitor of the imperial Chauhan Rajput dynasty that ruled large parts of northern India during the medieval period.
historical_references.context: Founder of the Chauhan Rajputs and progenitor of the imperial Chauhan Rajput dynasty

historical_references.reference: According to Hindu mythology, Kuldipsinh was a descendant of the lunar dynasty (Chandravanshi) of the Solar Dynasty (Suryavanshi). He is mentioned in various Hindu texts, including the 'Skanda Purana' and the 'Mahabharata', as a powerful and just king who ruled over a vast territory in present-day Rajasthan and Haryana.
